title: Rethinking and Red-Teaming Protective Perturbation in Personalized Diffusion Models

problem.claim: Personalized diffusion models are vulnerable to minor adversarial perturbations that substantially degrade fine-tuning on corrupted datasets.

gap.claim: Existing purification methods can break protective perturbations but often over-purify images and lose information.

contributions.claim: The work analyzes personalized diffusion model fine-tuning through shortcut learning and attributes the vulnerability to latent-space misalignment between images and text prompts.
The work proposes a red-teaming framework combining data purification with contrastive decoupling learning using noise tokens.
The work provides an evaluation framework for developing stronger protection against adaptive perturbations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an empirical demonstration that adversarial perturbations induce latent-space misalignment in the CLIP embedding space.
The authors report that extensive evaluation shows advantages over existing purification methods.
The authors report robustness against adaptive perturbations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Personalized diffusion models adapt text-to-image models to specific subjects with minimal training data.
Minor adversarial perturbations can severely degrade fine-tuning, enabling protective perturbations against unauthorized image generation.
Existing purification-based red-teaming methods may remove useful image information through over-purification.
The authors link the vulnerability to shortcut learning caused by perturbation-induced image-text misalignment and spurious associations.
The proposed framework uses restoration and noise-token contrastive decoupling, with reported advantages over existing purification and robustness to adaptive perturbations.

source_observation.claim: Perturbations can cause models to associate noisy patterns with unique identifiers during fine-tuning.

interpretation.claim: Robustness analysis should examine whether a model learns spurious perturbation-specific shortcuts rather than only measuring output degradation.

application.claim: For systems trained on perturbed data, inspect representation alignment and separate semantic concept learning from nuisance-pattern learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this mechanism generalizes beyond personalized diffusion models or the described perturbation setting.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines image restoration with contrastive decoupling using noise tokens to address purification and spurious noise learning.

interpretation.claim: Red-teaming defenses may benefit from combining semantic restoration with objectives that explicitly isolate nuisance patterns.

application.claim: When purification risks information loss, pair restoration with a learning objective that preserves personalized concepts while suppressing noise associations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when restoration or contrastive decoupling fails, or how much information each component preserves.

unknowns: Datasets, perturbation construction, and training configurations are unspecified.
Evaluation metrics, quantitative results, baselines, and statistical details are unspecified.
The adaptive perturbation threat model and robustness protocol are unspecified.
The relative contributions of data purification and contrastive decoupling are unspecified.
